gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: You ___ decide now — take your time and think it over.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' removes the obligation to act immediately: needn't decide.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: We ___ hurry — the doors close in five minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' expresses urgent advice: had better hurry.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better not be late again; the boss is getting tired of it.
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'had better' places 'not' after 'better': had better not be.

gaps.sentence: ___ you mind giving your seat to that elderly lady?
gaps.explanation: 'Would you mind + -ing?' is the standard polite request.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have brought a present, but it was kind of her anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' plus the participle means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have brought.
